newsitem.title: TURKEY: Denktash in Turkey for Cyprus missile talks.
newsitem.headline: Denktash in Turkey for Cyprus missile talks.

text.p: Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash arrived in Turkey on Monday for talks on a joint response to a bid by the Cyprus government to deploy Russian-made missiles on the island.
"The talks I will have with the president will give the message that Turkey will not take a step backwards on Cyprus," Denktash told reporters at Ankara airport.
Denktash, leader of the Turkish Cypriot breakaway state recognised only by Ankara, was due to meet Turkish President Suleyman Demirel later in the day.
Turkish officials have said the two sides may discuss setting up a joint military base in northern Cyprus, where Turkey has some 30,000 troops.
Turkey has threatened a military strike if the Cyprus government, based in the south, installs the S-300 anti-aircraft missiles, due on the island in around 16 months.

Denktash was confident of Turkish support. "What will happen if they put missiles all over the island? They will have great Turkey, with its population of 65 million, against them," he said. "Turkey will not leave Cyprus to the Greek Cypriots."
Cyprus has been divided since Turkey invaded in 1974 in response to a Greek Cypriot coup backed by Athens.
